note: E19: a route at its cap. The server runs at most --traverse-max-concurrent /traverse requests at once (1 here, with --http-threads 4 and -p 2); a further one is refused when its handler starts, before its body is parsed: HTTP 503 with Retry-After: 1 and {code: "busy", error, server_instance}, unwrapped and without usage on a single-graph and a multi-graph server alike (the shape of the loading 503, which has no code; server_instance names this process, so that a ledger that pinned another one sees the restart at once). Nothing of it ran and nothing of it was registered: GET /traverse/attempt/{attempt_id} and GET /requests/{attempt_id} answered 404 after it, and the same request sent again after Retry-After, once the slot was free, ran (200). Like the loading 503 it is no ground of the release rule. /resolve and /pattern refuse alike at their caps (--resolve-max-concurrent, --pattern-max-concurrent); every /traverse capabilities probe and GET /capabilities' multigraph block state the caps (max_concurrent). A real run of the E19 binary: a graph list with bact_other (the integration fixture of samples 05 and 23) and a slow pair whose walk held the one slot; the request is sample 05's with an id of its own.
